summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for left upper quadrant abdominal pain worsened by oral and tube feeding intake, different from prior ulcer episodes. After bowel rest and imaging, an EGD revealed a 10 mm gastrojejunal anastomotic ulcer. Initial tube feeding adjustments caused persistent pain, leading to discontinuation and initiation of TPN via PICC on hospital day 7. A small MRSA-positive pustule at the G-tube site was drained and treated. Feeds were retrialed on hospital day 12 with Peptamen Bariatric formula at a cycled rate of 60 mL/hr, which was well tolerated. The PICC was removed, and the patient was discharged home on enteral feeds, liquid pantoprazole twice daily, sucralfate, and an increased nortriptyline dose for pain. Follow-up was arranged with gastroenterology and surgery.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
Unspecified local infection of skin and subcutaneous tissue
